proposal: The Mandate recommends repealing the Inflation Reduction Act's Medicare drug price negotiation program, which it describes as government price controls that replace private-sector Part D negotiation, and pursuing other Part D reforms. Until repeal, it says an administration required to implement the law should do so prudently, minimizing its effects.

status_summary: The program has continued and is being put on a regulatory footing rather than repealed. A 2025 law (Public Law 119-21, signed 2025-07-04) expanded the program's orphan drug exclusion, which narrows its reach but leaves it in place. CMS issued final guidance for the third cycle on 2025-11-28 and on 2026-01-27 announced 15 selected drugs, the first cycle to include Part B drugs, plus one drug selected for renegotiation, with negotiated prices taking effect 2028-01-01; for the second cycle CMS reported agreement on all 15 drugs, with prices effective 2027-01-01. On 2026-06-16 CMS proposed to codify the program in regulation (new 42 CFR part 429; comments closed 2026-08-17 and CMS expects a final rule in fall 2026) and on 2026-07-20 issued draft guidance on putting 2028 prices into effect. Separately, CMS finalized the GLOBE model on 2026-10-02, a mandatory Part B rebate model benchmarked to international prices that takes effect 2026-11-30 and excludes drugs with a negotiated price. No bill repealing the program was examined.

timeline.event: Public Law 119-21 is signed (GovInfo dates it 2025-07-04); its section 71203 expands and clarifies the orphan drug exclusion in the Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program. CMS's 2025-11-28 final guidance (next entry) addresses it.
CMS publishes final guidance (90 FR 54692) for the third cycle (initial price applicability year 2028) and first renegotiation, continuing the program.

CMS announces the third cycle: 15 selected drugs, the first to include Part B drugs, plus one previously negotiated drug (Tradjenta) selected for renegotiation, with prices effective 2028-01-01. CMS also reports agreement with manufacturers on all 15 second-cycle drugs, with prices effective 2027-01-01 and estimated savings of about $8.5 billion (about 36 percent) had they applied in 2024.

CMS proposes (docket CMS-4215-P) to codify the program in 42 CFR part 429 and adjust Part D rules: selection of up to 20 drugs across Part B and Part D from initial price applicability year 2029, rules on the orphan drug exclusion, biosimilar delay requests, renegotiation and a temporary price floor for small biotech drugs. Comments closed 2026-08-17 (11,341 received); CMS expects a final rule in fall 2026.
CMS publishes draft guidance (91 FR 45278) on how manufacturers put negotiated prices into effect in 2028; comments were due 2026-09-18.

CMS publishes the final GLOBE model rule (91 FR 62936, effective 2026-11-30): a mandatory Part B drug rebate model benchmarked to international prices, running from 2027-04-01; it excludes drugs that have a negotiated maximum fair price in effect and is separate from the negotiation program.

title: Repeal the Medicare drug price negotiation program created by the Inflation Reduction Act
uncertainties: Federal Register documents were read through summarizing fetches (the proposed rule and GLOBE rule were read only through the first 100,000 characters). The first-cycle (2026 prices) results were not examined, and the third-cycle selection summary is slightly unclear on whether the 15 drugs split between Part B and Part D (the CMS release is described as including the first Part B drugs). The orphan drug exclusion change comes from CMS's description of Public Law 119-21 section 71203; the statute text was not read. No search was run for repeal bills or litigation over the program (several manufacturer suits exist in earlier cycles but were not checked). The Mandate also says to be prudent in implementing the law; I treat the orphan drug expansion as consistent with that and the Part B expansion and codification as inconsistent, which makes 'diverged' (0) a judgment call on the repeal recommendation rather than on the whole passage.
